name: Toothpaste on pimples
lead: Dabbing toothpaste on a pimple overnight is a long-circulating home remedy for acne. People use it as a cheap spot treatment because they expect it to dry out the blemish by morning, so the spot looks smaller and less inflamed [3].

The idea is often traced to older toothpastes containing triclosan, an antibacterial ingredient thought to help acne; the US FDA moved to limit triclosan in 2017 and, as of 2019, no toothpaste sold in the US contains it, according to Cleveland Clinic [3]. Modern toothpaste typically contains abrasives, fluoride, foaming surfactants, flavourings and sometimes antibacterial agents [1].

Cleveland Clinic dermatology resident Taylor Bullock describes toothpaste as made for the mouth and says its ingredients can irritate skin [3]. No clinical studies were found on toothpaste for acne, and Wikipedia's acne article does not list it among treatments [2].
infobox: Salicylic acid or benzoyl peroxide spot treatments [3]

paras: Typical toothpaste components include abrasives (8-20% of the product), fluorides, foaming surfactants, antibacterial agents and flavourants such as peppermint [1]. Sodium lauryl sulfate has been linked to oral tissue dryness and mouth ulcers in some people, and hypersensitivity reactions to polyethylene glycol-containing substances have been reported [1]. These observations concern the mouth and do not address facial skin.
Cleveland Clinic reports that triclosan was thought to help acne by killing bacteria, though its effectiveness was long debated [3].

Taylor Bullock of Cleveland Clinic says the original reasoning is outdated and that ingredients that help teeth can be too harsh for skin, listing redness, stinging, burning, irritation and inflammation, and saying the result can be a redder, more irritated pimple [3]. The article names drugstore spot treatments containing salicylic acid, which removes dead skin cells, or benzoyl peroxide, which targets surface bacteria, as alternatives [3].

card.summary: The classic overnight dab of toothpaste on a pimple; no studies were found and toothpaste is not designed for skin.
card.note: Ingredients such as surfactants and flavourings are reported to irritate oral tissue.

quick.overview:
Some people apply toothpaste to a pimple overnight, believing it dries the spot out.

No clinical studies were found, and standard references on toothpaste and acne do not describe this use.
quick.mechanism: Proponents point to drying ingredients such as abrasives and surfactants; no research confirms this effect on acne.
quick.risks: Sodium lauryl sulfate and other ingredients are reported to irritate oral tissues and cause sensitivity in some people.

chain: Toothpaste applied to a pimple overnight
Proponents expect drying and shrinking of the spot
angle.text: People dab toothpaste on a pimple hoping it will dry and flatten the spot before they are seen. This is a traditional home claim; dermatologists quoted by Cleveland Clinic say irritation is the more likely result [3].
